tier_rationale: The YU4's FCC grant (QKH-KANTOYU4) is filed simply as a 'Bluetooth Speaker' covering Bluetooth classic and BLE test modes — there is no Wi-Fi grant, and the rear panel's only inputs are RCA, 3.5mm AUX, two optical digital inputs, a USB charge-only port, and Bluetooth. The full 12-page user manual documents pairing, input selection, bass/treble/balance and standby entirely through the front-panel knob and included IR remote, with no app, no account, and no network step anywhere. A search for a Kanto companion app for this model turns up none — Kanto sells no software for the YU4 at all, so there is no vendor cloud for it to phone even if it wanted to.
the_unplug_test: There is no router in this speaker's life to begin with. It takes a turntable, a phone over Bluetooth, or a TV over optical, and turns it into sound from a knob and a remote. Nothing about it changes whether your network exists or not, because nothing on it ever asked for one.

repairability.notes: Passive right speaker is wired to the active left speaker with standard bare-wire speaker cable, and RCA/AUX/optical inputs use standard connectors; no proprietary connector locks the pair together.

sources.supports: Official user manual: full front/rear panel diagram (RCA, AUX, dual optical, subwoofer out, USB charge port, Bluetooth), remote control layout, and operating instructions. No app, account, Wi-Fi, or network step appears anywhere in the manual; USB port is explicitly labeled 5V/1A charge-only.

FCC grant for the YU4 (grantee Kanto Distribution Inc., filed as 'Bluetooth Speaker') covers Bluetooth classic and BLE test modes only; no Wi-Fi (802.11) authorization exists for this model, confirming Bluetooth is the device's only radio.
Manufacturer product page confirms current availability and input list (RCA, AUX, dual optical, Bluetooth); no companion app is offered or referenced anywhere on Kanto's site for this product.

open_questions: Price not confirmed this run — left null rather than spend search budget on it, per project policy.

Did not independently verify Kanto's full product-support site for an absence of any account system company-wide (e.g. a warranty-registration portal); the absence of an app specifically for the YU4, and the FCC grant showing no Wi-Fi module, are the load-bearing facts for D1 rather than a claim that Kanto operates no cloud anywhere in its business.
notes: Fills the empty 'powered speaker' subcategory and is the domain's first D1. Distinguish from Kanto's networked models (e.g. the Kanto Ren, which does add Wi-Fi and a Google Cast-based app) — this record covers only the plain Bluetooth YU4/YU2/YUMAX-style line with no network hardware at all.
